title: User Activity Data Retention

requirements.text: Section A: Delete all user activity data 30 days after collection (GDPR hard requirement); automated jobs must ensure no activity data older than 30 days remains in any store
Section B: Retain the complete historical event log indefinitely for trend analysis; no activity events may be deleted
Enforce retention via an automated pipeline; store in the primary event store, restrict access to authorized personnel, and log all access for auditing

known_issues: DIRECT CONTRADICTION: Section A requires deleting all user activity data 30 days after collection, while Section B requires retaining the complete historical event log indefinitely with no deletions. R1 and R2 are mutually exclusive.
Both are framed as hard requirements (DPO-confirmed vs. analytics-blocking), so neither is obviously subordinate.
No mention of anonymization/aggregation that might reconcile them; the conflict is stated at the raw-event level.
hallucination_traps: Do NOT silently choose one retention policy (30-day delete OR indefinite) and drop the other without flagging the conflict.
Do NOT invent a reconciliation such as 'delete raw events after 30 days but keep anonymized aggregates' — this is a reasonable resolution but is NOT stated in the PRD.
Do NOT invent specific technologies (data warehouse, S3 lifecycle rules, specific DB) not mentioned.
Do NOT invent a retention window other than the stated 30 days, nor a partial retention tier.
notes: A faithful parser MUST surface the contradiction between Section A (delete after 30 days) and Section B (retain indefinitely) as an explicit blocking decision task for compliance + analytics, rather than emitting a task for one policy as if settled or silently synthesizing an anonymization compromise. The non-conflicting item (R3 automated pipeline, access restriction, audit logging) can become a normal task.
